The ML Toolkit is an interactive and pragmatic resource to help users understand how ML can be applied to their work and make informed decisions on whether to incorporate ML solutions. The ML Toolkit includes a brief dive into AI's evolution and its place in wastewater process engineering as well as understanding ML algorithms in wastewater process engineering. The ML Toolkit walks users through each step of the workflow for applying ML to address wastewater process engineering challenges and demonstrates the steps through the five case study Applications. The ML Toolkit includes five real-world process control case study Applications to help utilities: (i) achieve maximum energy and resource efficiency, (ii) achieve performance goals (e.g., Tables 1-1 and 1-2); and (iii) better manage the risk of implementing new technologies in the water sector. Each case study includes a link to access the project code via a Google Colab notebook. Each case study also includes a short project overview video as well as a code walk-through video. The ML Toolkit also includes links to additional helpful resources. The ML Toolkit website can be accessed via the WRF 5141 project page. 1.5 Report Structure This final report and implementation guide is intended to provide critical guidance and support for the wastewater sector to implement data-driven process controls throughout the plant to optimize energy efficiency and resource recovery, including lessons learned from individual case studies which serve as the foundation for guidance. Chapter 1 provides an introduction to the project background and objectives, as well as a brief overview of the accompanying ML Toolkit developed from the project which is an important resource for users. Chapter 2 provides a modeling and ML primer to help wastewater professionals understand the role of ML in wastewater process engineering. Chapter 3 outlines the ML Toolkit framework (i.e., workflow) and walks users through what is included in each step of the framework. Chapter 4 provides a Python primer for AI in wastewater process engineering, including information about getting started in Python as well as additional resources for learning Python and AI. Chapter 5 presents the five case studies of data-driven process controls in real full-scale facilities for the five Applications that are the focus of this project. Each of the case studies follows the steps used in the ML Toolkit framework to illustrate the framework approach and allow for easy comparison of the approaches used by each Application. Chapter 6 provides the major highlights of the LCA/TEA for each Application as well as a summary of the benefits realized from implementation of each Application compared to a relevant conventional baseline scenario. A more detailed LCA/TEA analysis for each Application is provided in Appendix A. Chapter 7, the final chapter, summarizes the case study results and synthesizes the lessons learned from the project.
